transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

Since the water remains in the drum, the machine is waiting for the drain pump to empty it before it can proceed to the next stage (usually spinning). Please switch off and unplug the machine first for safety, then reach into the filter opening and try to spin the plastic fan/impeller by hand. Tell me if it turns freely or if you feel resistance or hear something clicking.

Hmm, I'm not sure about that one. When I cleaned the filter (twice now) there was only fluff in it, but I never tried spinning anything in there so I can't tell you if it's stiff or not. Is it likely to be the pump then? It does sometimes run for a second and then just stops.

It is possible it is the pump, but not necessarily because the motor has failed; often a small object (like a coin, hairpin, or piece of plastic) gets caught in the impeller blades behind the filter, causing it to jam intermittently. The next most useful check is to listen while it tries to work. Please start a Drain or Spin programme and tell me if you hear the pump humming or buzzing from that location, even if no water drains.

I haven't tried that, so I can't say if it hums or buzzes. It's fine most of the time, so I'd have to wait for it to stall again. All I've noticed is the pump sometimes runs for a second and then stops, and there's nothing odd to hear before that. Should I try a drain programme when it next stalls, or do it now while it's working?

You can try this now; there's no need to wait for it to stall again. Start a Drain or Spin programme and listen closely at the bottom front where the filter is. If you hear a steady hum but no water moves, something is likely jammed in the pump impeller. If it's silent or makes a grinding/clunking noise, the pump motor itself may be failing.

Ok, I'll give it a go with a drain programme now while it's working. Honestly I can't promise I'll be able to tell a hum from a grind though, and it's been fine today so it might not show anything. What if it sounds normal?

If the pump sounds normal but still doesn't clear the water, or if you can't hear it at all, the next most likely cause is a blockage further down in the drain hose. Could you check the grey drain hose at the back of the machine for kinks or crushing, and ensure the end isn't pushed too far into the waste pipe (which can create an airlock)? Also, try pouring a bucket of water directly into the filter housing to see if it drains freely by gravity.

I've already checked the hose and it's fine, goes into a standpipe and no kinks. I'm not keen on pouring a bucket of water in the filter housing though, and I won't be opening the machine up. Anything else I can try?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. And the machine is intermittent (fine one day, stuck the next), it points strongly to a small object like a coin or button that shifts around inside the pump housing. Because you won't be opening the machine up, we can't confirm this for sure, but if the pump motor itself were failing, it would likely happen every time rather than randomly. Given your constraints, I'd recommend running a drain/spin cycle whenever it gets stuck to see if it clears; if it keeps happening frequently, you will need an engineer to remove the back panel and check the impeller.
